scope: Focused stop-proof lifetime correction only. Parent owns final live, full suite, source, ledger and acceptance evidence.

diagnosis.source_defect: Completed stop names were local to QuiesceOwnedWorkersAsync. An observer failure discarded them, so an already stopped Unknown/disabled resource could be mistaken for a pending startup on the automatic fallback and explicit retries.
diagnosis.sibling_defect: Task.WhenAll throws after all stop tasks settle; successful sibling names were collected only after a successful aggregate, losing completed proofs when another stop failed.
diagnosis.interpretation: The stop command stages finished within the unchanged 30-second worker budget. Resource contention alone does not explain loss of retry progress. The source defect is reproduced independently with controlled real SDK notification/command services; the expired live control plane was not available for a fresh status observation.

correction: Retain completed stop proofs for the application lifetime, clearing only after application disposal succeeds.
After every stop group settles, collect each completed-success task sequentially in finally, even if another sibling failed.
Keep exact kernel-exit proof, pending-start fencing, retained failure ownership and existing deadlines unchanged.

behaviors: Real owned process exits before a controlled DCP unsuccessful result is accepted.
Snapshot remains Unknown with stop disabled.
An optional genuinely unsuccessful sibling stop still retains the completed Unknown sibling proof.
Observer failures retain infrastructure across automatic fallback and an explicit retry.
Each completed worker is stopped only once; pending worker fences and setup cancellation remain covered.

limits: No broad or live tests were rerun by this patch agent.
No running parent batch was signaled or changed; failed-session cleanup was performed separately by the parent.
This focused regression qualifies the retry protocol, not a new live-topology acceptance result.
